newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close weaker, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close weaker, seen consolidating.

text.p: Taiwan stocks closed slightly lower on Tuesday in narrow-ranged trade and brokers expected the market to consolidate around current levels in the near term.
They attributed slow sentiment to the fact that many share prices were recently at high levels.
Despite hopes for the central bank to further loosen monetary policy at a scheduled board meeting on Thursday, minor buying was limited in cement, rubber and food shares.
The weighted index lost 19.67 points or 0.31 percent to finish at 6,415.76. Turnover fell to T$40 billion from Monday's T$58.99 billion.

"There were hopes for further rate cuts, but I don't think the central bank will do it again that soon," said Albert Lin of Golden Securities. The central bank last cut commercial banks' reserve requirements on August 23 to boost the economy.
"It is only an excuse to maintain the upward momentum after previous gains," said Mike Tsai of Grand Cathay Securities, who added that he saw little chance for further rate cuts.

Reaction was mixed over the Securities and Exchange Commission's investigation into possible insider trding in British industrial conglomerate BTR Plc's sale of three major Taiwan petrochemical firms on Monday.
Union Petrochemical and USI Far East said on Monday they had agreed to buy BTR's controlling stakes in Taita Chemical, Asia Polymer and China General Plastics.
Union Petrochemical lost 40 cents or 1.25 percent to T$31.40, USI Far East fell 20 cents or 0.6 percent to T$31.20 and General Plastics lost 80 cents or 2.8 percent to T$28.50.
But Asia Polymer gained 50 cents or 0.92 percent to T$55 and Taita Chemical gained 10 cents or 0.32 percent to T$31.10.
Brokers expect prices to move narrowly in the near term, with interest centred on companies that have reported good first-half profits. -- Joyce Liu (2-5080815)
